Headteacher's Welcome
I am very pleased to welcome you to the West Somerset College website. Our website aims to offer you a wealth of information about our vision for the future and our many successes and achievements.
At West Somerset College we have high expectations for your child; we will support them to work hard, develop resilience, perform academically and flourish into young people who are fully equipped for the next stage in their learning journey, further education or the world of work.
At West Somerset College we have an exceptional team of dedicated staff who provide an inspiring and supportive learning environment. in order for them to achieve their aspirations.
West Somerset College students are resilient, responsible and respectful of others; we are immensely proud of them all.
I hope that this website provides you with a flavour of life at West Somerset College. If you wish for any further information, please do not hesitate to contact us.
Zoe Stucki

School Vision / Ethos
Responsibility. Resilience. Respect.
At West Somerset College, we believe every student is unique and full of potential. That is why we are committed to delivering a broad, balanced and ambitious curriculum, enriched with diverse opportunities that enable every learner to thrive—regardless of their starting point.
Our vision is to empower students to succeed on equal terms with their peers. Through high-quality teaching, meaningful enrichment and strong personal development, we support our young people to grow in confidence, capability and character, improving their social mobility and expanding their future opportunities.
When students leave West Somerset College, we want them to step forward as responsible, resilient and respectful citizens—equipped with the knowledge, skills and qualifications they need for the next stage of their journey.
As members of the West Somerset College community, we:
Take Responsibility for our choices and actions.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Sixth Form - West Somerset College
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Sixth Form
Without doubt, the short time a student spends in sixth form will probably be the most challenging time in their education. The courses they study, the demands they face and the adjustments they must make will bring with them great opportunities.
We are always delighted at the proportion of our students that choose to continue their study at West Somerset College Post 16. We believe that our success is directly linked to the aspirations of our students and the commitment of our staff to help them achieve their goals. The staff and the students pride themselves on the quality of teaching and learning at Post 16 and our consistently excellent and improving results validate this.
We have a team of very skilled mentors who will support students during their stay. They will guide and support students in terms of academic performance and will encourage them to take part in enrichment activities that will help them to develop wider skills, which are very important for progression to employment or HE. The College is a safe and secure environment in which to practice and hone these attributes. There will be a range of opportunities for students to participate in and we actively encourage all students to make a strong contribution to Sixth Form and wider college community.

Revision
Revision Advice for Students
Revision Advice for Students
At West Somerset College, we understand that effective revision is crucial for success in exams. To help you make the most of your revision time, we have put together some tips and strategies to keep you motivated and focused.
How to Revise
Using a variety of revision techniques will help you stay engaged and avoid burnout. It's essential to store your revision resources in an organized way, making it easy to find the information you need when you need it.
Refresher Cards
One topic per card, key points only. Colour code to make links and associations.
Testing
Ask family and friends to test you. Use previous examination questions. Choose topics and questions that you are uncertain about. Get used to working under timed conditions. Check your answers. Do some questions with your notes and others without.
Learning Maps
Start in the centre with the topic title. Main points about topic as thick branches, smaller points as smaller branches. Don't crowd the paper. Use colour, pictures and symbols.
Highlighting Notes
Must be selective. Highlight only key words and ideas. Colour code to make links and associations.
Posters/Post-it Notes
Display around your study area. Particularly useful for important vocabulary and key statistics.
Key-word Listing
Begin with a blank, landscape piece of A4 paper. Choose a topic and write down what you know, following the instructions below. Use a different colour for each section.
Coping Skills for Examinations
Positive Talk
Avoid negative discussion with your friends. Don't be put off or intimidated by anything other people say.
Check Equipment
Make sure you have everything you need with you. Pens, pencils, rubbers, felt tip pens, calculators etc. Know what you are allowed to use.
Arrive in Time
Not too early, not too late. Avoid hysterical discussion and keep calm.
Keep a Clear Head
Things won't always go perfectly, but if you keep your mind focussed and as relaxed as possible you should be able to adapt to any awkward questions or challenging situations. If you get stuck, re-read the question, think back to studying the topic in and out of class and don't just give up.
If Things Go Badly?
It's not the end of the world!
Revision Tools
Students at West Somerset College can use GCSEPod to help with their revision.
Useful Links
For further revision advice and support, visit the following websites:

Tutor Reading Programme
Reading for Pleasure at West Somerset College
We value reading for pleasure at West Somerset College and encourage our students to do the same. Our reading programme takes place each Monday and Friday morning during tutor time and offers all students in Year 9 and Year 10 the opportunity to read and enjoy a book together with their tutor.
Our Tutor Reading Programme
Whilst undertaking tutor reading, students will not be required to study the texts or complete work set based on them; they will be asked only to follow the text as it is read to them, and to listen, enjoy and discuss the topics raised as appropriate.
Each tutor group will cover at least four texts across the year and all texts have been chosen in order to introduce students to a range of perspectives and ideas they may not experience in everyday life or through their independent reading.
Many of the texts cover sensitive topics such as race, bereavement, gender, equality, violence, discrimination, mental health, war, politics and religion. As such, our Tutor Reading Programme is designed to be both a window and a mirror: each book is carefully selected to allow students to hold a mirror up to their own selves through the rich and wonderful texts that they read, while also reflecting upon their own thoughts, feelings, and place within the world.
It is also intended that these texts become a window out into the world of wider human experiences, different customs and beliefs as well as new and enriching knowledge which will unlock more windows and doors for them in the future.

Work Experience
Year 10 and 12 Work Experience: Monday 13 - Friday 17 July 2026
Year 10 and 12 students have the exciting and beneficial opportunity to complete a week of work experience at West Somerset College.
The Benefits of Work Experience
Undertaking a week of work placement can be a very valuable experience for students. It deepens their understanding about what a career in the placement area involves, helps them to understand their own strengths and areas to develop in relation to employability skills and can also give them first-hand experience on which to draw in future applications/interviews.
Encouragement and Support
We encourage all our students to undertake work experience. During the work experience week there will be no Year 10 or 12 lessons. Those students who have not managed to find a placement, even with our support, will stay in school and carry out GCSE revision.
Finding a Placement
Past experience has shown that it is best for students to find the placement themselves. We will of course support them throughout the process. Many very successful placements arise out of personal contacts that students have through their friends or relations. Students must be able to get themselves to the placement, so it is generally best if it is a local placement, but some students do go further afield where families can make the necessary arrangements. In school tutors will be encouraging their Year 10 students in finding a placement and if more help is needed then appointments can be made with Mrs Ahern.
Health and Safety Requirements
After placements have been found, a form needs to be filled out by the parent or carers. Each placement also has to be assessed to make sure that it complies with safeguarding and health and safety requirements. This is a legal requirement.
Getting Started
Parents - please start to discuss work experience with your child to get thinking about suitable opportunities. We look forward to supporting you both through this exciting process!

Attendance
Why getting to school on time, every day, matters!
Missing out on lessons leaves children vulnerable to falling behind.
We seek to ensure that all our pupils receive a full-time education which maximizes opportunities for each pupil to realise their true potential both socially and academically.
Over a period of five school years, a pupil with 90% attendance will have missed half of a whole year of schooling. Similarly, pupils with poor punctuality miss valuable lesson time and, if it happens regularly, progress will be jeopardised.
We expect outstanding attendance for all, however we do recognise that there are times when pupils will absent from school.
If attendance drops below 97% the school will contact parents immediately to put a plan in place to make improvements.
This form is for students who are feeling mildly unwell or experiencing mental health concerns but are still able to attend school. It allows us to record how they are feeling so that staff can monitor their wellbeing and provide appropriate support throughout the school day.

Free School Meals
At West Somerset College, we believe that every student deserves access to nutritious meals, regardless of their financial situation. Our school is committed to providing free school meals to eligible students, helping to support their academic success and overall well-being.
Eligibility Criteria
In England, children are eligible to receive Free School Meals (FSM) if they are in receipt of any of the following benefits:
Income Support
Income-based Job Seekers' Allowance
Income-related Employment Support Allowance
The guaranteed element of State Pension Credit

Parents Evenings
You can book for Parents Evenings on the Parent Arbor App
On the main page of your arbor app, if the booking has been opened, you can select Guardian Consultations.
You can also use the menu. Click the menu icon at the bottom left of your screen, then select Guardian Consultations.
This will take you to the consultation page. You can see the dates you can book meeting slots within, and also see when you can book these slots until.
You can download a list of the meetings you have booked as a PDF by clicking on the green Download my meetings button.
To book a meeting, click the available meeting at the bottom of the screen.
Click on the Time slot drop-down and choose the time you would like to attend the consultation, and which and which guardians will be attending. Top Tip: You can select from any guardians the school has linked to the child, but only guardians with parental responsibility can log into Parent Portal.
If you can't select a time slot, it means the staff member has not been given a period of availability - get in touch with your school and ask them to add this into their setup to enable you to book a slot.
Make sure at least one guardian is ticked or you won't be able to click the Book Time Slot button.
You will be asked to confirm your choice and you'll be sent an email confirmation.
The page will then show that your booking has been successful.
You can edit your booking by returning to the page and clicking on your booking. Select a different time slot and click Reschedule meeting to change your slot.
Click Amend guardians to remove one of the child's guardians or add them back into the meeting.
You won't be able to remove all guardians from the slot, and you'll receive this error.
If you've unticked yourself as the attending guardian, you'll have the option to book a separate meeting slot if your school allows this.
If you want to remove an incorrect booking or add yourself back into the original booking, get in touch with us and we will amend this for you.
